sentence: The top drops… and the bottom doesn't move at all.
claim: Until the collapse of the turns reaches it, the bottom end of the released slinky does not move.
source_title: Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012), arXiv:1208.4629

sentence: Slowed down, the top coils pile up from above, while the bottom floats there.
claim: The turns collapse from the top end, bunching together, while the lower turns are still at rest.
source_title: Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012), arXiv:1208.4629

sentence: For about a third of a second.
claim: The total collapse time is typically about 0.3 s for real slinkies; in our ideal 60 cm model it is √(2ℓ/g) = 0.35 s.
source_title: Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012), arXiv:1208.4629

sentence: Nothing down there has been told.
claim: The bottom is unaffected until the release of the top end has been communicated to it.

sentence: The pull of the spring doesn't jump to the other end; it travels down the coils, like a wave.
claim: The collapse time equals the time a wave front takes to propagate down the slinky, communicating the release of the top end.
source_title: Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012), arXiv:1208.4629

sentence: Until the news arrives, the bottom has no reason to move.
claim: Before the wave front arrives, the tension at the bottom is unchanged, so the bottom stays at rest.
source_title: Cross and Wheatland, 'Modeling a falling slinky', Am. J. Phys. 80, 1051 (2012), arXiv:1208.4629

sentence: It falls the whole time, like a dropped ball.
claim: After release the only external force is gravity, so the centre of mass of the slinky accelerates downward at g from the first instant (air ignored).
source_title: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, 9.6 Center of Mass; Cross and Wheatland 2012

sentence: The top rushes down, the bottom waits, and the average is a plain fall.
claim: The centre of mass is the mass-weighted average of the coils' positions; it falls like a free body while the top moves and the bottom waits.
